Head access/ slide out mattress to allow for easy access of the neonate for CPR/intubation. 2 access doors wit h 2-4 port doors (elbow-operated) and 1 iris port. IV Pole and LED lamp. 2. 2. Modes and alarms - air mode and servo mode should be available. Audib le and visual alarms for power failure, disconnected skin sensor, air circula tion, high and low temperature. Temperature sensors for air and skin temp erature which can read with an accuracy of ±0.1°C. 5 reusable skin temper ature probes of +/- 0.1C accuracy should be supplied with EACH machine. 3. 3. Incubator body - Provision for mounting two cylinders (for air and oxyge n). Handles on both sides for moving the equipment. Rubber bumper that protects all the sides of the equipment. Should have tray for keeping emer gency equipment and supplies. Provision for mounting pulse oximeter and T-piece resuscitator and transport ventilator. Mattress with anti-stress foa m and waterproof cover made out of non-toxic materials. 4. 4. Power - electrically operated with rechargeable battery. Power system s hould be capable of charging from mains (AC/DC). Battery back-up of at le ast 4 hours 5. 5. Pulse oximeter (masimo/ nellcor, with wrap-on neonatal reusable probes ) for continuous patient monitoring with provisions for mounting the same. Digital display of skin temperature & oxygen concentration 6. 6. A transport ventilator should be supplied along with incubator, with prov isions for mounting the same. Transport ventilator for neonatal use, should be turbine/compressor driven, not requiring external air cylinder, with inter nal rechargeable battery backup of at least 3 hours. Modes available: press ure controlled ventilation, CPAP, and NIV. Should allow the following set pa rameters: PIP, PEEP, rate, Ti, and FiO2 (21–100%) - 1 no with each incubator 7. 7. Battery or inverter should be able power the transport incubator and als o support the running of humidifier and transport ventilator for short transp ort of up to 3 hours.
